content.title: About
content.content: The Chocolate Coated Cereal Bar NFS combines whole grains, nuts and dried fruit, covered with a layer of milk chocolate. It is designed as a quick snack that provides energy through carbohydrates and healthy fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The bar contains whole grains such as oats and whole wheat, preserving most of the dietary fiber.
The chocolate coating is made with cocoa butter rather than vegetable oils, enhancing taste and texture.
It often includes sunflower and pumpkin seeds, which are rich in magnesium and zinc.
NFS (Not From Scratch) indicates minimal processing of the ingredients.
Each bar is individually wrapped, making it convenient for travel and active lifestyles.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: A mix of complex carbs and simple sugars in the chocolate coating quickly replenishes glycogen stores.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grains and dried fruit provide dietary fiber that supports normal digestion.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Nuts and seeds supply monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Grains are a source of B1, B2 and niacin, which aid metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains magnesium, iron and zinc, supporting muscle function and the immune system.

items.title: Nut and seed allergy
items.content: The product contains nuts and seeds that may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The chocolate coating adds simple sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The bar is relatively calorie‑dense; excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Gluten presence
items.content: Contains wheat, making it unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar can be eaten straight from the wrapper as a quick snack. It can also be sliced and added to yogurt, oatmeal, or used as a sweet element in baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, consume within 7‑10 days. Discard if a rancid odor develops.

chicken-leg-drumstick-and-thigh-grilled-.title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, grilled with sauce, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh prepared on the grill with a flavorful sauce. The skin is removed and not consumed. The meat is tender, juicy, high in protein and contains a modest amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken legs and thighs are popular in barbecue dishes because of their rich flavor.
Grilling imparts a smoky aroma and caramelizes the sauce on the surface.
Removing the skin reduces saturated fat, making the dish more diet‑friendly.
Chicken meat is a good source of vitamin B6, which is involved in protein metabolism.
Traditional grill sauces often contain honey, soy sauce, garlic and spices.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth, repair and supports the immune system.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Skin‑less preparation lowers saturated fat content, benefiting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 aids amino‑acid metabolism and supports nervous system function.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium has antioxidant properties and supports thyroid function.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: High protein content helps maintain a feeling of fullness for longer.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper cooking or storage can allow bacteria such as Salmonella to grow.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain high salt levels; people with hypertension should watch portions.

items.title: High grilling temperatures
items.content: Excessive charring can create harmful compounds like acrylamide and heterocyclic amines.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a main dish, slice for salads, sandwiches, or add to rice and vegetable sides. Drizzle extra sauce or garnish with fresh herbs if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked product in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before consumption.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey soufflé is a light, airy dish made from eggs, finely chopped poultry, dairy ingredients and seasonings. During baking the mixture rises, creating a delicate, almost creamy texture. Soufflé is often served as an appetizer or a light main course.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soufflé originates from French cuisine, where the word “soufflé” means “blown up”.
Achieving the airy structure requires carefully beating egg whites to stiff peaks.
Soufflé can be made sweet (with chocolate, fruit) or savory (with meat, cheese, vegetables).
Traditionally it is baked in small ceramic ramekins.
Soufflé loses its shape quickly after leaving the oven, so it is served immediately.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken, turkey and eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When made with lean poultry and modest amounts of cream, soufflé can be relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and poultry contain B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Dairy components add calcium and phosphorus, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Easily digestible protein
items.content: Egg protein is readily absorbed, making soufflé a good option after illness or when higher protein intake is needed.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Soufflé contains a large amount of eggs, which can trigger reactions in people allergic to egg whites.

items.title: Undercooking risk
items.content: If not cooked through, especially with chicken, harmful bacteria may remain.

items.title: Hot serving temperature
items.content: Soufflé is served hot; caution is needed to avoid burns.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt or ready‑made sauces can raise sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve soufflé straight from the oven, often with a light sauce, fresh herbs, or a simple salad. It can be eaten with a spoon or cut into portions for a starter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in the oven or a steam bath to retain the airy texture.
